The programs below grew out of the research described on the [Research](research.qmd)
page. They are written to be verified: every new capability comes with a test case, and
the double-porosity code reproduces the single-porosity one in the limit case.

## GEOMECH3D

Three-dimensional finite element program for coupled poroelastic analysis — solid
deformation and fluid flow in the framework of Biot's theory. Written in Fortran, in
development since 2021. It reads models prepared with the GiD® problem type
[AugustoPoroelastico.gid](https://github.com/augustobopsinborges/AugustoPoroelastico.gid)
and writes results back to GiD® for post-processing.

[Repository →](https://github.com/augustobopsinborges/GEOMECH3D){.btn-ab}

## GEOMECH3D-DP

Finite element program for **double-porosity** poroelasticity: Biot's theory extended to
two porous systems, the rock matrix and the network of joints, with fluid exchange
between them. The coupled displacement–pressure–pressure problem leads to a symmetric
indefinite system, solved in three dimensions. Developed separately from GEOMECH3D so
that it could be verified independently; its companion problem type is
[GEOMECH3D-DP.gid](https://github.com/augustobopsinborges/GEOMECH3D-DP.gid).

[Repository →](https://github.com/augustobopsinborges/GEOMECH3D-DP){.btn-ab}

## GeoMicroLab

Python library to implement, audit, verify and compare micromechanical models of porous
materials and fractured rock. Every formulation states its hypotheses, documents its
equations and declares its limitations, and the documentation distinguishes, line by
line, what is implemented, tested, verified mathematically and validated against
experiments.

<!-- [Repository →](https://github.com/augustobopsinborges/geomicro-lab){.btn-ab} -->
